name: Michigan

default_limits.basis: MCL 257.627: 25 business districts/residential subdivisions, 55 trunk line and county highways (incl. gravel), 70 limited-access freeways

fine.notes: Civil infraction; each district court sets amounts. Example (58th Dist., fine+costs): 1-5 over $105, 6-10 $115, 11-15 $125, 16-25 $135, 26+ call court.

court_costs.notes: Court may add costs up to $100, plus $40 justice system assessment (MJI table, 2021). Often bundled into court's total.

points.notes: MCL 257.320a. Reckless driving = 6 pts. One court lists interstate speeding as 0-4 pts; statute shows no such exception.

zones.work_zone: 45 mph where a lane is closed unless otherwise posted (MCL 257.627(6)).
zones.school_zone: Fines doubled for moving violations in school zones (58th Dist. Court).

court.reason: No pay-by-schedule amount at 26+ over in sampled court; 4 points from 16+.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (misdemeanor) - conduct-based, no speed number

trucks.notes: Trucks 10,000+ lb, truck-tractors, combos and school buses: max 65 where posted limit is higher (MCL 257.627(4)).

sources.title: MJI civil infraction monetary sanctions table

notes: Speeding is a civil infraction; no speed-based criminal threshold. Residential 25 applies to subdivisions/designated residential streets, else 55. Freeway 75 and some 65 trunk lines are posted. Statute 1-pt tier reads 'more than 1 but not more than 5'. Fine data from one court only.
